names.note: The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name link 1421 as the day page prints it, «Максим Азийский, мч.», with the rank word left off; his life page is headed «Мученик Максим Азийский». The day's own line declines him «Мч. Максима (ок. 250).», with no epithet at all; the epithet is the name page's. `fk.mjs` on «Максим Азийский» returned NONE before the write.

death.note: The day line closes him with «(ок. 250)», about 250, and his life page gives the reign instead: «Святой мученик Максим пострадал при императоре Декии (249 - 251)». The two agree, so the display is the day line's approximate year and the bounds are the reign the life names. The page gives no birth and no age.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 14 мая ст. ст. — «Мч. Максима (ок. 250).»

attestations.note: **Checked against every Maximus the corpus holds before writing**, because there are eighteen: all `saints/maximus*` folders were listed with their types, their venerated days and their years, and not one stands on the menologion's 14/5 or is a layman trader of Asia — the nearest in year are `maximus-companion-of-olympias`, a martyr of 249–251 the Greek keeps on 15 April in a company, and `maximus-companion-of-terentius`, 250, of the Carthaginian company; `fk.mjs` on «Максим Азийский» returned NONE. **No `office` and no clerical type**: the life makes him a layman who lived by trade. **No `locations`**: the name page's Азийский is a province and the life names no city. The day page prints hymns for two of the saints it heads and nothing under his name. azbyka.ru was not read.
